report.summary: Read the full change, including the part cut from the diff: Artifacts helpers, egress (workspace and CI modes), RepositoryCiDO, CI runner, native merge op and tempod git.merge/ci.checkout, issue/label/comment stores and handlers, agent issue tools, D1/DO migrations, deploy/wrangler bindings, Mac views and tests. Artifacts calls match the generated worker-runtime.d.ts contract. Egress injects a write token only for the trusted remote's Git endpoints, strips caller credentials and uses manual redirects. CI mode forwards only upload-pack with a read token and blocks receive-pack. Ownership checks precede every Artifacts or DB call. Issue numbering, PR duplicate guards, CI token or stale-result guards and merge lost-ack recovery are idempotent. The 0007 migration backs up and restores every cascading dependent. No blocking defect found. I did not run typecheck/lint/test because this run is read-only and turbo writes caches and CLAUDE.md. Four non-blocking findings.

findings.text: On a retry after a lost tempod acknowledgement (push succeeded, response lost, so pushedMergeSha was never saved), prepareArtifactMerge still sees the PR open and the merge gate runs again before tempod's operation-marker recovery. If the pipeline revision changed in between, newestRun finds no run for the head SHA under the new revision and the recovery is refused, contrary to spec 10 ('A merge already pushed (lost acknowledgement) is still recovered without the gate'). Confirm with a test: push succeeds, response lost, pipeline saved, then retry merge.

evidence.why: The gate is checked before tempod can detect the already-published merge commit, so a gate change between push and retry blocks recovery.

findings.text: README says Artifacts repositories have no CI checks integration, but this change adds tab 10 project CI with checks, merge gating and a Checks tab in both clients.

evidence.quote: Artifacts repositories have no CI checks integration yet.
evidence.why: Contradicts docs/10 Project CI.md and the shipped RepositoryCiDO and Checks UI.

findings.text: A module-level afterEach(vi.restoreAllMocks) in a cases file imported into forge.test.ts runs after every case in that file, including concurrent cases from other modules. No other forge case uses spies today, so it is harmless now, but a future concurrent spy would be restored mid-test. The same applies to artifacts-workspace.cases.ts in forge-workspace.test.ts.

evidence.why: This is a global mock reset at file scope, shared with concurrent cases in the same test file.

findings.text: If revoking the import's initial token fails, the error is swallowed. The token is never persisted or returned, but it stays valid until it expires (binding default TTL is 86400 s).

evidence.quote: // Imports can return before a disposable repository handle is available.
evidence.why: The spec says to revoke where the service permits; a transient failure here leaves a live write token, which is acceptable only because it is never stored.

checked.risk: Real contracts (Artifacts binding, Containers outbound interception, tempod protocol, git)
Idempotency and state (merge op, issue numbering, PR creation, CI tokens and results, migrations)
Security (ownership, token scope, secrets in container env and logs, CI read-only egress)
Build and runtime environment (bindings, DO classes, image file mode, versions)
Tests (sleeps, shared spies under concurrency, observable waits)
